articles.headline: 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' will require all GA public schools to install mobile panic alert systems beginning July 1
articles.excerpt: Beginning July 1, Georgia's 'Ricky and Alyssa's Law' requires every public school to deploy mobile panic-alert devices, putting an emergency button in the hands of every teacher and administrator and linking directly to first responders. It honors two victims of school violence.

articles.headline: Minnesota's anonymous school threat reporting system law begins July 1
articles.excerpt: A Minnesota law taking effect July 1 requires every public school district and charter school to provide an anonymous way to report threats via app, website, or hotline, giving students and staff a faster channel to flag danger to administrators before it escalates.

articles.headline: July 1: New Mississippi laws take effect today
articles.excerpt: Among the new Mississippi laws taking effect July 1: anyone 18 or younger who commits a crime with a firearm will now be automatically charged as an adult. Backers frame the tougher stance as a deterrent to the weapons increasingly turning up on and around school campuses.

articles.headline: Two teens arrested after stolen gun allegedly brought to Wicomico Middle School
articles.excerpt: Maryland's Wicomico County Sheriff's Office arrested two teens after a stolen handgun was allegedly brought onto Wicomico Middle School's campus. School staff alerted deputies, who recovered the weapon and filed multiple firearm and weapon-on-school-property charges.

articles.headline: Violence against teachers is more widespread than you think
articles.excerpt: An Atlanta Journal-Constitution examination finds violence against teachers is far more common than official tallies suggest, with many educators bitten, hit, or threatened by students and cases going unreported, fueling burnout and departures from the profession.

articles.headline: Elyria High School student arrested after bringing gun to campus, running away, prompting lockdown
articles.excerpt: An Elyria High School student brought a gun onto the Ohio campus, ran from officers, and triggered a precautionary lockdown before being arrested, police said. No one was hurt, and the district credited its safety protocols with enabling a swift response.

articles.headline: Spanberger signs bipartisan school-safety, student support bills into law
articles.excerpt: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed a bipartisan package of school-safety bills, including one permitting school boards to equip teachers with wearable panic alarms that alert law enforcement during a classroom emergency, alongside expanded staff safety and threat training.

articles.headline: Kentucky bill toughens school violence disciplinary actions
articles.excerpt: A Kentucky measure to protect teachers and school staff from violent students advanced with broad support, requiring a minimum 12-month expulsion for students in grades 6-12 who intentionally injure school employees, plus mandatory reporting of assaults to law enforcement.
